title: Dominic and the Summer
premise: Ten years ago, Mirabel Sandoval survived a ferry accident that killed her sister, then vanished into a life of sea turtle research on a quiet coastal town, answering only the anonymous letters that arrived each summer from someone who knew her before. When Dominic Reyes—the brother of the man who died saving her, and the voice behind every letter—moves in next door without revealing himself, their slow-blooming friendship is built on a secret that could shatter them both. As nesting season peaks and Mirabel finally pieces together who he is, she must choose between the loyalty she owes her sister's memory and the truth that could give her a second chance at love; in the end, she lets him stay past the last train, choosing to be seen rather than safe.
about_author: Sebastian Kavanagh is a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who writes love stories set against working coastlines and the people who repair themselves there. He lives off-season in a town much like the one in this book, where he volunteers with a sea turtle rescue program.

chapters.title: The Counting Season
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Opening on nesting beach at dawn, we learn she counts turtles to avoid counting losses, especially her sister Elena's death ten years ago. A new neighbor's moving truck rattles her carefully ordered world. Emotional beat: guarded routine disrupted.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He unpacks boxes of letters he never sent and photographs of a girl he's searched for, watching Mirabel through the fence line. He knows exactly who she is; she doesn't know him. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by deception.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their first real conversation over a shared fence about a stranded hatchling. Mirabel finds him easy in a way that frightens her; Dominic nearly confesses twice and swallows it. Emotional beat: first spark, first lie of omission.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Signed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Flashback to writing the first letter after the accident, guilt-ridden, unable to sign his name because his brother Mateo died pulling Mirabel from the water. Emotional beat: the origin of the secret.

chapters.title: Nest 47
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She invites Dominic to help monitor a nest, breaking her rule against letting people close. His gentleness with the hatchlings undoes something in her. Emotional beat: trust tentatively extended.

chapters.title: What Elena Would Say
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The anniversary of the wreck approaches; she visits the memorial bench and tells Elena about the new neighbor, feeling disloyal for smiling. Emotional beat: grief versus budding hope.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We learn his lease is temporary—he came to say what he needed to say, then leave. The nightly train becomes a ticking clock. He asks Mirabel, almost casually, when she last left town. Emotional beat: deadline established.

chapters.title: Storm Watch
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A tropical storm forces them to sandbag the research station together through the night, soaked and laughing, hands brushing. Almost-kiss interrupted by a hatchling emergency. Emotional beat: intimacy accelerating.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Helping Dominic unpack, she glimpses an old photo: two brothers and a teenage girl on the ferry dock—herself, Mateo, and a boy whose face she can't quite place. Unease plants itself. Emotional beat: suspicion's first thread.

chapters.title: Hatchling Run
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Guiding baby turtles to the sea, he tells Mirabel about losing a brother without naming him or her. She shares her survivor's guilt for the first time in years. Emotional beat: mutual confession, still incomplete.

chapters.title: Midsummer Letter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. This summer's anonymous letter arrives—and she recognizes phrasing Dominic used verbatim on the beach. She says nothing, testing him with a detail only the letter-writer would know. Emotional beat: the trap quietly set.

chapters.title: He Knew the Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dominic answers her test perfectly, quoting the letters back without realizing. She spends a sleepless night cross-referencing ten years of envelopes with his handwriting samples at the station. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into certainty.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She confronts him: 'You're the letters.' Dominic admits everything—Mateo was his brother, he wrote every word, he moved here to finally earn forgiveness he was never sure she'd want. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief colliding.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Wound
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Furious and heartbroken, she accuses him of ten years of surveillance dressed as tenderness. Was any of it real? He leaves the answer unanswered and walks toward the train station. Emotional beat: rupture.

chapters.title: Elena's Box
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Grieving, she opens her sister's keepsake box and finds Elena's diary: Mateo had told Elena he loved her; the brothers were coming to visit that summer. Her anger softens into understanding—everyone was protecting someone. Emotional beat: reframing the past.

chapters.title: The Empty Platform
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the station, bag packed, he can't board. Flashbacks of Mateo telling him, 'If anything happens to me, don't let her disappear.' He misses the last train deliberately. Emotional beat: choice made.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. During a night survey she finds a tagged turtle she's tracked for years returning to nest—proof things come back when the conditions are right. She runs home through the dark. Emotional beat: decision igniting.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Both POVs. She finds him sitting on his porch in the dark, ticket unused. No speeches—she sits beside him, shoulder to shoulder, and says, 'Stay.' The word costs her everything and gives it back. Emotional beat: climax resolved in stillness.

chapters.title: Telling the Truth Out Loud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Together they visit Elena's memorial; Mirabel introduces Dominic properly, aloud, releasing the secrecy. She reads one of his letters to the sea. Emotional beat: grief integrated, not erased.

chapters.title: Nesting Rights
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He signs on as a station volunteer; the town begins to know him as more than the new neighbor. Mirabel teaches him to tag nests, their old fence-line distance gone. Emotional beat: rebuilding on honest ground.

chapters.title: The Season Turns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Final nest hatches at dawn; they release the last hatchlings together as the season ends. She realizes she stopped counting turtles somewhere along the way and started counting days instead. Emotional beat: transformation complete.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Both POVs, closing. One year later: a new letter arrives—but this one is signed, addressed to both of them, from a young volunteer they mentored. On the porch, past the last train, Mirabel lets someone stay. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution, love chosen daily.
